---
description: One command per API call, over a folder of Oracle queries.
title: Command line
---

`ichnos` has one command per API call, so it prints nothing that a Python caller cannot get.
Every command takes the corpus, a folder of query files or one file, as its first argument, and writes to stdout or to the file that `-o` names.

The examples on these pages run at build time on the synthetic corpus in [`tests/fixtures/oracle_synthetic/queries`](https://github.com/ozanozbeker/ichnos/tree/main/tests/fixtures/oracle_synthetic/queries), under the name `queries`.

```{python}
#| label: help
#| echo: false
from _scripts.example import ichnos

ichnos("--help")
```

## Commands

Each command calls one function or walk of the API:

| Command | Writes | API call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`dbml`](dbml.qmd) | The DBML file of the inferred schema. | `dbml(graph)` |
| [`summary`](summary.qmd) | One line per table and report. | `summary(graph, owner=..., keyword=..., budget=...)` |
| [`neighborhood`](neighborhood.qmd) | The tables within some relationships of one or more centers. | `dbml(graph.neighborhood(...))` |
| [`join-path`](join-path.qmd) | The shortest join paths between two or more tables. | `dbml(graph.join_path(...))` |
| [`upstream`](upstream.qmd) | Where the values of a table, a column, a report or an output column come from. | `dbml(graph.upstream(...))` |
| [`downstream`](downstream.qmd) | What a table or a column feeds. | `dbml(graph.downstream(...))` |
| [`unparsed`](unparsed.qmd) | Each query that ichnos could not read. | `graph.unparsed` |

## The corpus

In a folder, ichnos reads every file whose suffix is `.sql`, in every subfolder, and skips a file or folder whose name starts with `.`.
`--suffix` replaces `.sql`, and it can repeat.
Each file decodes on its own: a BOM picks the codec, a file with no BOM decodes as UTF-8, and a file that fails UTF-8 decodes as cp1252, or as the codec `--encoding` names.

## Options

Each option mirrors an API parameter, with the API's name, values and default:

| Option | Default | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-o`, `--output PATH` | stdout | every command |
| `--suffix SUFFIX` | `.sql` | every command |
| `--encoding NAME` | `cp1252` | every command |
| `--budget N` | `8000` | [`summary`](summary.qmd) and the slice commands |
| `--detail compact\|full` | `compact` | the slice commands |
| `--examples` | off | the slice commands |
| `--indirect first_hop\|all` | `first_hop` | [`upstream`](upstream.qmd) and [`downstream`](downstream.qmd) |
| `--depth N` | `1` | [`neighborhood`](neighborhood.qmd) |
| `--owner NAME` | none | [`summary`](summary.qmd) |
| `--keyword TEXT` | none | [`summary`](summary.qmd) |

The slice commands are [`neighborhood`](neighborhood.qmd), [`join-path`](join-path.qmd), [`upstream`](upstream.qmd) and [`downstream`](downstream.qmd).
A choice must match exactly: `--indirect first_hop`, not `first-hop`.

## Output

Every command writes UTF-8 with `\n` line endings, on every OS.
On Windows, PowerShell re-encodes what it pipes, so write a slice with `-o` and copy the file, as the [README](https://github.com/ozanozbeker/ichnos#paste-a-slice-into-a-chat-on-windows) shows.

## Exit codes

The CLI exits with one of three codes:

- `0`: success.
- `1`: a user error, as one line `ichnos: <message>` on stderr, with no traceback.
- `2`: a usage error, such as an unknown option or a missing argument.

A name that matches nothing is a user error, and the message names up to three close matches:

```{python}
#| label: exit-code
#| echo: false
from _scripts.example import ichnos

ichnos("neighborhood", "queries", "SALES.ORDER")
```

Two more lines can go to stderr, and neither changes the exit code.
When the core of a slice exceeds the budget, ichnos writes the whole slice and says so.
When any query is unparsed, every command except [`unparsed`](unparsed.qmd) writes one line with the count.
